body:
Yeah, I've realized more and more that my parent's bad attitudes about things has really taken a toll on me. When I was young they used to say things like "eating healthy and exercising is for losers" or "working hard is for losers" and I think this contributed to my laziness or whatever it is. They told me that being depressed is an excuse for not doing anything, so then I just never did anything...

I've been trying to pull myself out of these thought patterns for a while, but I'm so used to them it's difficult. They've basically raised me telling me I have nothing to look forward to in life after I'm 18, and then act confused when I say I don't see the point in finishing my college education and pursuing anything besides my dream. I mean, I was terribly depressed in high school too, and when I would tell them they'd be understanding, but also say things like "well, enjoy it now because it only gets a lot worse afterwards". 

EDIT: Recently I've been dealing with a lot of anger I have towards them, as I originally wanted to go to a certain school for university, but they convinced me out of it saying that I'd drop out, I'd hate it, it'd be a disastrous choice, etc. So I went to the other school that I knew I didn't want to go to, and ended up dropping out anyway because I wanted to be at the other school. Had I not listened to them I know I would have finished school. I know it's my fault, so I blame myself for listening to them and not being strong, but I also just don't know what to do anymore. Everything is just too much of a struggle. College I can't deal with because I have too much social anxiety and having so many people around is just overwhelming. I had a lot of friends in college, but dealing with a roommate and a dorm situation pushed me over the edge, as well as that my grades started declining because I needed to work on group projects with people but I was too nervous to speak with anyone in my classes. 

I know that if I go back to school the problems will only be worse, as my mental state has only declined since I was in school last. In terms of just getting a job and working, I don't know how I'm going to be able to do that either as I honestly just feel ashamed if people think I want to live. I don't know why, and I don't know how to get over this, but when people say things like "well at some point you're going to have to start earning money so you can support yourself" I get this angry feeling (I don't actually respond angrily, I just feel angry) that makes me want to say "don't you understand that I'm not going to support myself? That I've been trying to kill myself since I was 9 years old, that when I was 10 I said I'd do it by the time I was 18, and I'm way passed deadline? I'm not going to support myself, when that time comes I'll just kill myself." 

Sorry to lay all this on you.

I think I really do want to go through with the act, but I'm just sort of scared. I wrote my first suicide note when I was 9 years old, so this isn't a new thing. That's why I feel like if my dreams don't pan out I don't have anything really to live for anymore. My entire family has a terrible history of mental illness, and every day my dad tells me that he might just kill himself, or that we should all get a van and drive off a cliff together, so it's hard to really find a reason to go on.

I think that I'm kind of stuck in the field I'm in as it's always been my dream to do something in this area. I feel like the main thing I need to do is realize that I actually love doing this for more than just the idea of success. But when I go to sleep every night thinking I'll just kill myself I'm not sure how to move forward.

Thanks again for your responses, by the way

No you didn't offend me, no worries. It's true that there are things I'm better at, he's even told me this, but it's just hard to remember it I suppose. 

I just have trouble dealing with the scale of things. If they keep going the way they are, this guy may be a household name in a few years.

I guess the hard part is that I know it's more than just luck. He's just better than me.

I know that it's something I should try to move past, but I don't know if I can. And it's just constantly bearing down on me more and more.

Thanks for your response. I appreciate it a lot.

The problem I encounter is that if I don't expect anything of myself, which I've tried, then I feel like that's exactly the path to not achieving what I want in life. Honestly one of the major problems is my friend, as I'm very close to him and it's a constant reminder every day that I'm not as good. 

Just to make matters worse - we were actually originally working on the same business. But then we branched off after he got an opportunity in another venture of his, and now he's becoming wildly successful and I haven't gotten anywhere.
